prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

Green Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (≤500 words)

The Greens frame 2019 as a crossroads: climate breakdown, Brexit turmoil and democratic failure demand a decisive shift. They propose a decade-long Green New Deal (GND) to reach net-zero by 2030 while tackling inequality, alongside reforms on Europe, democracy, public services, and fair taxation.

Core Green New Deal (≈£100bn+ per year, plus UBI; capital via public borrowing; private co‑investment expected):
- Energy: Rapid expansion of wind (≈70% of UK electricity by 2030), plus solar, tidal, hydro and geothermal; grid upgrades, storage, demand management; end fossil subsidies; rising Carbon Tax on extraction/imports; ban fracking; oppose new nuclear; boost interconnectors.
- Housing: Insulate every home; deep retrofit 1m homes/year; 100,000 new Passivhaus-standard council homes/year; heat pumps and low‑carbon heat networks; solar for 1m homes/year; higher standards for new builds; raise rented homes to EPC A by 2030.
- Transport: Make public transport cheaper than driving; electrify rail; reopen lines/stations; shift freight to rail; empower councils over buses/trams; £2.5bn/year for walking/cycling; EV sale ban by 2030 plus nationwide charging; 20mph default in residential areas; cancel HS2, new runways, and road‑capacity schemes; frequent flyer levy; end flight ads.
- Industry & Circular Economy: Grants to replace high‑carbon kit; CCS for steel/cement; 10‑year warranties and right to repair; cut F‑gases; near‑100% recycling infrastructure; ban most single‑use plastics; support UK clean-tech manufacturing; £2bn/year for skills and apprenticeships; regional mutual banks.
- Food, Farming & Forestry: Ten‑year shift to agroecology; 700m trees; halve pesticide use and ban most harmful; rewilding and hedgerow restoration; agroforestry on 50% of farms by 2030; urban food growing; meat/dairy tax phased in to fund farmer transition; GM moratorium; flood resilience via nature-based solutions.

Universal Basic Income and Incomes:
- Phase-in UBI: adults £89/week; pensioners £178/week; supplements for disabled, lone parents, children; keep housing benefit for recipients; 35 hours/week free childcare from 9 months; Living Wage £12 (incl. 16–21s); rent controls and end no‑fault evictions.

Europe:
- People’s Vote with Remain option; reform EU institutions for transparency, citizen initiative, and MEP legislative power; defend freedom of movement; EU carbon border tariff; humane refugee policy.

Democracy & Government:
- Proportional representation; votes at 16; elected second chamber; citizens’ assemblies and written constitution; Digital Bill of Rights; media plurality; Carbon Chancellor with annual Carbon Budget; Future Generations Act; split Home Office into Ministries for Sanctuary and Interior; shift defence to Security and Peace; end arms export promotion; empower and fund local government (+£10bn/yr; free home care for over‑65s; £3bn climate adaptation fund).

Public services:
- NHS: +£6bn/yr (to 2030); end internal market; community health centres; mental health parity; free contraception; PrEP access.
- Education: +£4bn/yr; smaller classes; end high‑stakes testing/Ofsted model; formal schooling from 6; restore arts/sport; scrap tuition fees and write off £9k‑era debt; boost FE/adult learning; climate and nature education.

Nature & Animals:
- Ecocide law; stronger planning protections; new environmental watchdog; peat and water protection; right to roam; 30% UK waters fully protected by 2030; urban greening; animal sentience, ban hunting/snares, end badger cull, phase out animal testing, end factory farming and live exports.

Justice & Drugs:
- Halve prison population via reduced short sentences, restorative justice, women’s centres, youth services; end war on drugs: legalise/regulate with harm reduction, medical heroin, legal cannabis/social clubs, minimum alcohol pricing.

Tax & Spend:
- Consolidated Income Tax merging major personal taxes; tax wealth like work; Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax/Business Rates; Corporation Tax 24%; anti‑avoidance clampdown; support small business (regional banks, faster payments, VAT cuts for hospitality/culture, higher Employment Allowance). Cancel Trident, HS2, road‑building, Help to Buy; no airport expansion.

Funding:
- New taxes and savings ≈£124bn + £29bn/yr; capital borrowing ≈£94bn/yr; Carbon Tax ≈£76.7bn/yr; UBI net cost ≈£86.2bn/yr. Aim: a fair, green economy with wellbeing over GDP.
